title: Jozimine A(2), a Dimeric Naphthylisoquinoline (NIQ) Alkaloid, Shows In Vitro Cytotoxic Effects against Leukemia Cells through NF-kappaB Inhibition.
authors: Damiescu, Roxana; Yucer, Rumeysa; Klauck, Sabine M; Bringmann, Gerhard; Efferth, Thomas; Dawood, Mona
one_liner_zh: 该文研究二聚体生物碱Jozimine A2通过抑制NF-kappaB信号通路发挥抗白血病作用，虽涉及分子对接预测配体与NF-kappaB蛋白的结合，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且未涉及TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法上可部分借鉴。
abstract: Naphthylisoquinoline (NIQ) alkaloids are rising as a promising class of secondary metabolites with pharmaceutical potential. NF-kappaB has already been recognized as a significant modulator of cancer proliferation and drug resistance. We have previously reported the mechanisms behind the cytotoxic effect of dioncophylline A, an NIQ monomer, in leukemia cells. In the current study, we have investigated the cytotoxic effect of jozimine A(2), an NIQ dimer, on leukemia cells in comparison to a second, structurally unsymmetric dimer, michellamine B. To this end, molecular docking was applied to predict the binding affinity of the dimers towards NF-kappaB, which was then validated through microscale thermophoresis. Next, cytotoxicity assays were performed on CCRF-CEM cells and multidrug-resistant CEM/ADR5000 cells following treatment. Transcriptome analysis uncovered the molecular networks affected by jozimine A(2) and identified the cell cycle as one of the major affected processes. Cell death modes were evaluated through flow cytometry, while angiogenesis was measured with the endothelial cell tube formation assay on human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). The results indicated that jozimine A(2) bound to NF-kappaB, inhibited its activity and prevented its translocation to the nucleus. In addition, jozimine A(2) induced cell death through apoptosis and prevented angiogenesis. Our study describes the cytotoxic effect of jozimine A(2) on leukemia cells and explains the interactions with the NF-kappaB signaling pathway and the anticancer activity.
abstract_zh: 萘基异喹啉（NIQ）生物碱正逐渐成为一类具有药物开发潜力的次级代谢产物。NF-kappaB已被确认为癌症增殖和耐药性的重要调节因子。我们此前已报道了dioncophylline A（一种NIQ单体）在白血病细胞中产生细胞毒性效应的机制。在本研究中，我们考察了jozimine A(2)（一种NIQ二聚体）对白血病细胞的细胞毒性作用，并与另一种结构不对称的二聚体michellamine B进行了比较。为此，我们采用分子对接 (molecular docking) 预测这些二聚体对NF-kappaB的结合亲和力，并通过微量热泳动 (microscale thermophoresis) 进行验证。随后，在CCRF-CEM细胞和多药耐药CEM/ADR5000细胞上进行了细胞毒性实验。转录组分析揭示了jozimine A(2)影响的分子网络，并确定细胞周期为主要受影响过程之一。通过流式细胞术评估细胞死亡模式，同时利用人脐静脉内皮细胞（HUVECs）的血管生成管形成实验测量血管生成。结果表明，jozimine A(2)与NF-kappaB结合，抑制其活性并阻止其向细胞核转位。此外，jozimine A(2)通过凋亡诱导细胞死亡并抑制血管生成。我们的研究描述了jozimine A(2)对白血病细胞的细胞毒性效应，并解释了其与NF-kappaB信号通路的相互作用及抗癌活性。
